result.note: Tests the MSMED (Amendment) Bill 2026 on delayed-payment timelines, TReDS for CPSEs, and the recovery, decriminalisation and Udyam provisions.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, passed by Parliament in August 2026:
items: It mandates that mediation in delayed-payment disputes must be completed within 90 days.
If a buyer's challenge to an arbitral award is pending for more than six months, courts must release at least 50 per cent of the awarded amount to the MSE supplier.
It raises the share of an arbitral award that a buyer must deposit with the court when challenging it from 50 per cent to 75 per cent.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong: buyers already had to deposit 75 per cent of an award, but its release to the supplier was left to judicial discretion. The bill adds a floor of 50 per cent release once a challenge has been pending for over six months.
questions.source: Now, if the challenge sits pending for more than six months, courts must release at least 50 per cent of the awarded amount to the MSE supplier upfront.

questions.prompt: Under the MSMED (Amendment) Bill, 2026, passed in August 2026, all Central Public Sector Enterprises must route their payments to MSMEs through which platform?
questions.explain: The bill requires all CPSEs to pay MSMEs through TReDS, an invoice-discounting platform. It also nudges state governments to put their own enterprises on it.
questions.source: It also requires all Central Public Sector Enterprises to route their MSME payments through the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS), an invoice-discounting platform, and nudges state governments to put their own enterprises on it too.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the MSMED (Amendment) Bill, 2026, passed by the Lok Sabha in August 2026:
items: It allows a mediated settlement or arbitral award to be recovered as an arrear of land revenue through the district administration.
It makes registration on the Udyam Registration Portal mandatory and fee-based for all MSMEs.
It retains criminal conviction as a penalty for failing to register or supply information.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Only statement 1 is correct. The Udyam portal gets statutory permanence as a free, voluntary platform, and failures to register or supply information are decriminalised into graded penalties, starting with a warning for a first instance of wrong information.
questions.source: The amendment also gives statutory permanence to the Udyam Registration Portal as a free, voluntary digital platform, and formally incorporates the twin criteria of "investment in plant/machinery" and "turnover" for MSME classification into the Act.
